newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds end week with a whimper.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds end week with a whimper.

text.p: *Australian bonds closed little changed after having failed to sustain an initial rally in another low volume session and in sharp contrast to how the market started the week.
*Market sees slim data calendar next week.
Australian bond yields ended the day little changed after having failed to sustain an initial U.S. led rally in another low volume session and in sharp contrast to how the week started.
"The market's just drifted into the weekend. We've seen some buying this afternoon, but not sufficient to alter the flow of the market," one trader said.
The absence of key data this week has been blamed for the slack activity of the past few days, and the indicator calendar is again extemely thin again next week.

The market had started the week with a bang amid a combination of a strong U.S. rally, the June futures close out and hopes of a further cut in official interest rates, which took 10-year bond yields to their lowest level in 3-1/4 years.

There has subsequently been a mild correction from the sub-7.0 percent level on the October 2007 benchmark, although policy easing speculation in the run up to the July 1 Reserve Bank board meeting is expected to underpin the market going into next weekend, traders said.
September bill futures are all but factoring in a 1/4 point easing at 94.85, equating to a cash rate of 5.15 percent.

Spreads to the bloc were fairly mixed and failed to follow through an initial narrowing to the U.S. The market lost ground to Canada, which rebounded with the Canadian dollar on Thursday, but N.Z. yields rose on comments by N.Z. Treasurer Peters, saying the markets were overly optimistic on fiscal forecasts.
